blocks: ### T87 (make-only refused a guard file's name written in a scratch tree as a guard file written from the shell, found by T79 on 2026-11-21: `guard_file_hooks::held` held a path by its name alone (`/Makefile`, `/dev/work-budget.json`, ...), so `printf x > /tmp/q/Makefile`, a builder's `T=$(mktemp -d); ...; printf ... > $T/Makefile` (tx#953, ux#2204) and a copy of `dev/work-budget.json` into a `$(mktemp -d)` preview (ux#1106, ux#1107) were refused, measured 2026-11-21 (`/tmp/t79/probes-mk.jsonl` through T79's binaries); on the guard log, 110 of make-only's 745 guard-write refusals and 11 of guard-file's 180 held a guard file's name under `/tmp` alone, measured 2026-11-21 (item 4))

decisions.summary: A path whose real path (existing part's links resolved) lies under /tmp or $TMPDIR and in no project tree (TREES: /diagram with its clones, /host-l7r-repo; CLONE_MAIN for tests) is no guard file; a $TMPDIR of /, home or a place holding it counts for none.
decisions.why: The task is a check refusing good work (110 make-only and 11 guard-file refusals of scratch fixtures, measured 2026-11-21), a defect under XIV; freeing scratch by real path, so a link into a clone is the clone's, fixes it without opening any project tree's guard file (both replays: no verdict changed outside scratch).

decisions.summary: Every place outside scratch keeps HEAD's reading by name, not only project trees: /Makefile (what the walk makes of $UNSET/Makefile and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/Makefile) and ~/.claude/settings.json stay held.
decisions.why: The task frees scratch fixtures; nothing asked frees places outside scratch. The brief's third rule keeps HEAD's reading for a path the walk cannot place, and HEAD's binary refuses echo x > $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/Makefile which the walk reads as /Makefile (measured 2026-11-21, shapes1.txt), so a list of project roots alone would let that write through; ~/.claude/settings.json is a real guard file registering the GM's hooks on 8 events (measured, the file read). Holding these keeps the enforcement real.

decisions.summary: make-only lets a write the walk placed in scratch overrule the text patterns hit by hit (statement paired with walk segment by its words); a write the walk cannot place or see beside it stays refused as at HEAD.
decisions.why: Mechanism of the same fix; narrower than a command-wide clear, and pinned against the let-through a command-wide clear produced (shapes3/4).

decisions.summary: The Python patterns no longer read a program the walk judged whose guard files' names all land in scratch; a program that chdirs is read from / and never freed.

decisions.summary: A command naming CDPATH keeps HEAD's by-name reading throughout (no hit cleared, no program freed).
decisions.why: Closes a let-through the fix would otherwise open (a clone write placed in scratch by a walk that does not read CDPATH, measured 2026-11-21, shapes7.txt); CDPATH stands in none of the 9,646 corpus rows or 925 refusals, so it keeps no good work refused.

decisions.summary: A command holding a worktree add keeps HEAD's by-name reading throughout; 17 logged rows of the 110 stay refused this way.
decisions.why: A worktree add makes a project repository's worktree in scratch before any .git pointer shows it, so at the guard's reading the place cannot be told from scratch: applying the scratch rule there is not possible without the pointer. The rows it keeps refused are writes into a project's worktree, whose commits reach the repository - not the scratch fixtures the task is for - so holding them serves the task's purpose and the GM's 'real enforcement' rather than gutting it.

decisions.summary: A git worktree in scratch of a project repository is a project tree (nearest .git read, gitdir/commondir followed, held where its real path lies in a project tree); 18 logged rows into standing worktrees and 4 corpus rows stay refused that the first fix freed.
decisions.why: It keeps refusals that a literal 'nothing under /tmp is held' would free, so it is ruled, not waved through. Purpose-level: the task's purpose is that scratch fixtures, which reach no project, are not refused; a project repository's worktree under /tmp is not scratch in that sense, since its commits reach the repository (pointers read, measured 2026-11-21, worktrees.py), and freeing its guard files would let a project's guard files be changed from the shell and committed - the opposite of the GM's 'make sure all of the enforcement is real enforcement'. The session ruled it on a review note, but the ruling rests on that purpose and is pinned red first.

decisions.summary: With other work uncommitted in the clone, make land runs whole in a persistent landing worktree <clone>-land at the clone's HEAD, under a lock, seeded with the clone's kept results; the clone then takes the landed tip (update-ref, merge-tree/commit-tree, three-way merge-file, conflict moves nothing, exit 4).
decisions.why: A design for a [perf] task under FR-013 (the landings). It narrows nothing the GM asked: the gate still judges the tree pushed, the push's dirty-tree refusal and the stamp's disk key are unchanged, and the two other ways are measured and rejected on their costs.

decisions.summary: While something runs, the Stop hook refuses a stop when fewer than L7R_BUILDERS (GUESS 3) builders run and next_independent names an open task never started, after no open task, touching no running task's named files; escape is make set-down F= WHY=.
decisions.why: Adds a refusal in service of the builders' loop; it carries a reasoned, recorded escape and a named compliant command, and red-first is recorded (350/2 then 352). Narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: next_independent takes performance work first across every active feature, then the rest, feature-first then each active feature by its last task-start.
decisions.why: This is FR-013's own clause: the Stop hook's start-the-next names an open performance task before any other, across active features. The plan corrected an earlier feature-first ordering that broke it (r1 red, r2 green).

decisions.summary: Where the task the Stop hook names is not performance work, its named make task-start carries PERF_LATER_OK - which happens only when every open performance task is started, waits on an open task, or overlaps a running task's files.
decisions.why: This narrows how far FR-013's task-start refusal reaches in practice, so it is ruled. It uses FR-013's own escape, of a reason, recorded, for the case that escape names: a performance task that cannot start now because it waits on another task's landing (or is already running). The hook names a non-perf task only after no performance task can be started. Leaving slots empty in that case would not get performance work done any sooner, and would undo the GM's purpose ('doing those first makes everything after them faster'), which is ordering, not idling. Each start still needs the escape typed in and logged.

decisions.summary: Overlap is read from a task line's named files or *_hooks modules against running tasks' edit lines, with specs/, .git/ and the ledger excluded and common basenames matched only with a path; a line naming nothing fails toward a start.
decisions.why: A design detail of the dispatch rule; its stated cost (two builders in one crate) is judged by T86's closing checks. Narrows nothing asked.
